newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori leaves Peru for talks on hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori leaves Peru for talks on hostage crisis.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori left on Friday for talks in Canada with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to analyse the 45-day siege at the Japanese ambassador's home where Marxist rebels hold 72 captives.
Government negotiator Domingo Palermo, Interior Minister Juan Briones Davila and five government party legislators, including congressional president Joy Way accompanied Fujimori.

Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani and Canada's ambasssador to Peru, Anthony Vincent -- two members of a commission set to supervise talks between the government and rebels -- also travelled to Canada. The Red Cross -- the final member of the commission -- did not send a representative to the meeting, scheduled to take place Saturday in Toronto.

Fujimori and Hashimoto agreed to hold the summit following criticism from Tokyo that provocative police manoeuvres at the residence were putting lives at risk. Before leaving Fujimori said the meeting was aimed at achieving "a very close coordination" between the two leaders.

About 15 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels seized hundreds of guests when they stormed the mansion Dec. 17 during a diplomatic reception. They released most of the captives but kept those they considered the most important bargaining chips, including Fujimori's brother, top government and security force officials, two ambassadors, and about two dozen Japanese diplomats and businessmen.
